title: Normalized quotient completion realizes the actual reduction-limit adjunction
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E$ a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $W$ a scheme such that $\ell$ is invertible in every residue field. Let $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ be the actual completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], let $t$ be its constant uniformizer section [lem-a1-principal-koszul-strict-replacement], and let $C_R$ be any normalized universal principal quotient completion model [def-pur-principal-quotient-completion-model]. There exist an actual coefficient derived-system calculus $A$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], normalized ordinary and derived unit models $M,N$ [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model], and a natural isomorphism $\alpha:C_R\simeq A.\mathrm{reduction}\,\mathrm{limit}$ carrying the entire principal quotient unit to the actual adjunction unit. For every flat-term K-flat complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] there is an isomorphism $\theta$ from its strict principal quotient tower to the restriction of $M.\mathrm{quotient}(P)$, with $q_n\theta_n=\mathrm{augmentation}_M(P)\pi_n$ for every positive quotient index. Moreover $C_R.\mathrm{counit}_P$ followed by $Q(\mathrm{roosF}(\theta))$ and the normalized comparison of $N$ equals $\alpha_{QP}$. Thus the identification fixes the entire cone comparison and every tower transition, not merely its finite-level projections. Site and coefficient universes are independent, exactly as in the Lean signature. The normalization predicates are those of [def-pod-completion-scalar-formulas].

proof.text:
take the normalized ordinary and derived models from the completion-unit
strict-quotient theorem. At level n identify the sheaf cokernel of multiplication
by the (n+1)-st uniformizer power with the residue sheaf through its projection.
Tensor with a flat-term K-flat P. The cokernel equations show that these maps
commute with all quotient transitions and carry the quotient augmentation to
M.augmentation. Apply the strict signed Roos functor, preserving both coordinates.
Its counit on K-flat complexes computes the universal completion. Localization on
flat-term K-flat representatives therefore gives alpha naturally. Its counit
normalization is the last displayed equation. Applying that equation to the
augmentation, whose shifted coordinate is zero, gives the actual adjunction unit
as a whole morphism; descent gives the equation on every derived object.

lean.statement:
theorem quotientAdjunctionRealization
    [∀ x : W, Invertible (l : W.residueField x)]
    (CR : @Model.{t + 1, t, max u (t + 1), max u (t + 1) + 1}
    W.ProEt inferInstance (essentiallySmallSelf.{u} _)
    (Scheme.ProEt.topology W) inferInstance
    (integralCoefficientAbSheafify.{t, u} W)
    (integralCoefficientAbLocallyBijective.{t, u} W)
    (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E W)
    (integralTowerHasDerivedCategory l E W)
    (PrincipalKoszulStrictReplacement.uniformizer l E W)) :
    ∃ (A : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E W)
      (M : CompletionUnit.OrdinaryModel l E W)
      (N : CompletionUnit.DerivedModel l E W A M)
      (α : CR.completion ≅ A.reduction ⋙ coefficientSequenceLimit l E W),
      ModelData.QuotientRealization l E W A M N CR α
